newsitem.title: USA: Witco cutting 1,800 jobs, closing 15 factories.
newsitem.headline: Witco cutting 1,800 jobs, closing 15 factories.

text.p: Witco Corp. said Thursday it would close a third of its factories and cut 1,800 jobs, more than a quarter of its work force, in an overdue move to cut costs to compete in the speciality chemical business.

The Greenwich, Conn.-based maker of speciality chemicals for cosmetics, packaging and other products said it would take a pretax charge of $421 million for the restructuring, environmental and safety compliance and other items.
Witco officials said the moves were meant to cut costs by more than $200 million a year by the end of 1999.
But industry analysts said Witco was playing catch up with other chemical companies that have been slashing costs for a decade.
"It's an overdue response to the pressures of the marketplace for better financial returns," said James Wilbur, chemical analyst at Smith Barney in New York.

Under the plan, Witco will cut its manufacturing plants from 46 to 31 and consolidate distribution and administrative centres. As a result, it will lay off 1,800 of its 6,800 employees, the company said.
Witco said it plans to invest $600 million in the next three years to modernise its remaining facilities, add capacity and upgrade its worldwide information systems.
Founded in 1920, Witco was a family-run business for decades. Bill Wishnick, the son of the founder, retired as chairman in 1990 but remains on the board of directors.
The current chairman, E. Gary Cook, joined in June of this year, and analysts had expected some belt-tightening.
"The restructuring is necessary to achieve the efficient, productive, competitive and agile company necessary to meet the ever more demanding needs of our global customers," Cook said in a statement.
Most of the plant closings will occur in North America, with Europe and Asia relatively unaffected, Witco Vice President Lloyd Moon said.

Moon said he did not know yet where layoffs would occur, adding that the company would offer outplacement services and enhanced severance packages to the affected employees. The company's 4,100 U.S. employees include 643 in Connecticut.
The company produces speciality chemicals for makers of cosmetics, household, automotive, agricultural, packaging and food products.
The restructuring was meant to cut fixed costs by 20 percent and other costs by as much as 10 percent, officials said.
Witco's stock added 87.5 cents to close at $31.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
